subject: array images for core exons only?

messages.author: 544a2f5526cc67ef
messages.subject: array images for core exons only?
parts:
When making residual or weight images using ArrayExplorer, is there a
way to plot only core exons?

Thanks,

victoria

messages.author: a5f6afcbe5b17914
messages.subject: Re: array images for core exons only?
parts:
Hi,

this is most likely related to the fact that calculateResiduals() (and
weights are then calculated from the residuals), first *copies* the
original CEL file, and then update the signals used in the PLM. In
other words, if the PLM is only fitting PMs, the signals for the MM
cells will be ones in the CEL file going into the PLM. Same, if you
only fitting a subset of the units or unit groups, then the non-fitted
ones will get the values from the input CEL file. This is a non-
wanted behavior. In have updated calculateResiduals() so it will
create an empty CEL file, that is, all non-fitted signals will get
value zero (one could argue that they should be NAs, but I have to
leave that for the future because that requires a more detailed
investigation of side effects). The above will be available in the
next version of the package.

Cheers

Henrik

On Mar 15, 5:53 am, xvw...@stat.berkeley.edu wrote:
> When making residual or weight images using ArrayExplorer, is there a
> way to plot only core exons?
>
> Thanks,
>
> victoria

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: array images for core exons only?
parts:
Hi Henrik,

If you first call getResidualSet(plm) it also sets up .CEL files for the
residuals. Would these be blank? (So that then when you then call
calculateResiduals() it would update these blank files, so is a
work-around until you have your update, which I assume hasn't come out
yet?).

I also ask, because I notice that unlike many of the other functions,
calculateResiduals doesn't have something like
'rs<-getResidualSet(this)' at the beginning. Instead it checks for if
the file exists and if not manually creates it (by copying as you said
below) and names the file with an appropriate tag. I have been writing
my own calculateResiduals function and have found this slightly unrobust
for programming. I have two different kinds of residuals that I give
different tags to and this means I have two places that define what my
tags should be -- if I change my mind later as to the names of the tags,
I have to remember to update the calculateResidual file. This may be
what your update will do, but I thought I'd mention it before you
release the new version.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: array images for core exons only?
parts:
Hi,
Just a further note on this. Calling getResidualSet() before
calculateResidual does set up blank cel files when I do it (i.e. zero
residuals), but then calculateResiduals() won't update them because it
thinks that because the file exists, the residuals have already been
calculated. So you always have to call calculateResiduals() first, it
seems (or choose force=T).
Elizabeth

Yes, getResidualSet() creates CEL files (to hold residuals), if
missing. In the current version these CEL files are copies of the
data files, but in the next version of the package these are created
from scratch and will be blank (zeros).

> what your update will do, but I thought I'd mention it before you
> release the new version.

I'm not sure if I follow/understand you here. For any PLM the error
terms are well defined, so I cannot see how different kinds of
residuals can be calculated. Are you talking about a model with
different error terms? If so, we should really discuss how to extend
the current ProbeLevelModel class with a new subclass handling
hierarchical models. I don't think it would fit into the current
design of ProbeLevelModel.

Henrik

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: array images for core exons only?
parts:
Hi,

thanks for this. Yes, the whole story about calculating residuals is
not 100% consistent with how the rest of the package works. There is
a need for a mechanism in calculateResiduals() that detects
non-calculated residuals much like what fit(..., units="remaining")
does. This will be possible first in the next version when residuals
are zero if not calculated. For now, yes, you have to use

calculateResiduals(..., force=TRUE)

to calculate the residuals in case you already created the residual
files using getResidualSet().

Calculating residuals is a special case; ideally I would like to store
the residuals at the same time as you fit() the PLM. Then, if not
wanted, the user can always delete the residual files manually,
because they take up a lot of disk space. If wanted later, the PLM
then have to be refitted (or we keep calculateResiduals() for
convenience). It boils down to a design question. I appreciate any
creative feedback on this.

/Henrik
